title: Fractional CTO for Small Business | Vestis Solutions
description: A fractional CTO for small business owners: connect the tools you already use, clean up your CRM, and automate the busywork. No new software pitch.
h1: A fractional CTO for small business owners who are tired of double entry
intro: You have a CRM, a scheduling app, estimating software, a phone system and QuickBooks, and none of them talk to each other. Your office types the same customer in three places. Every software salesperson says their tool will fix it. A fractional CTO for small business helps you decide what to keep, connect what you have, and stop paying for what you don't use.
definition: A fractional CTO is a part-time technology leader who makes the tech decisions for a business without a full-time executive. For a small business, that usually means choosing and connecting business software, cleaning up the CRM, and adding automation where it saves real hours.

sections.h2: What kind of fractional CTO I am, and what I'm not
paras: Some fractional CTOs lead engineering teams and build apps. That's not me. If you need custom software written, you need a software engineering lead.
I'm the owner's partner for business systems: the tools that run your sales, scheduling, jobs and billing. I help you make the decisions, connect the pieces, and get your team using them.

sections.h2: Work with the tools you already use
paras: I don't sell software, and I don't push a platform. Most businesses already pay for good tools. The problem is that they sit in separate boxes. I connect what you already use, and only recommend a change when a tool is truly holding you back. Any new software needs your approval first.

sections.h2: What a fractional CTO for small business should fix first
paras: When tools don't talk, leads get lost between the form and the follow-up call. More marketing on top of that only adds more mess. So I fix the plumbing first, then turn up the volume.
Systems are one part of a wider partnership that also covers getting found on Google and in AI answers, a sales process review, and four 30-minute owner sessions a month.

Partnerships start at $3,000 a month, with up to 12 delivery hours for meetings, setup and support. We start with 90 days, then continue month to month. I'm based in Charlotte, NC, and work with owner-led businesses locally and across the US.

faq.q: Does a small business need a fractional CTO?
faq.a: A small business needs one when its tools have become a daily drag and nobody owns the decisions. If your team retypes data, leads go missing between systems, or you keep buying software that doesn't stick, a part-time tech partner pays off. If your tools already work together, you probably don't.

faq.q: What does a fractional CTO do for a small business?
faq.a: For a small business, a fractional CTO decides which tools to keep, connects them, and adds automation where it saves time. My focus is business systems like the CRM, scheduling, estimating, phones, forms and accounting. I don't build custom apps or manage developers.

faq.q: How much does a fractional CTO cost?
faq.a: Fractional CTO costs vary by scope and hours. My partnerships start at $3,000 a month and include systems work alongside SEO and AEO, a sales process review and four owner sessions. Any new software, and its cost, needs your approval before it's added.

faq.q: Will you make me switch to new software?
faq.a: No, I work with the tools you already use. I don't sell or resell any platform. If one tool is truly holding you back, I'll explain why and what the options are, and the decision stays yours. Any new software, and its cost, needs your approval first.

faq.q: Can you build a custom app for my business?
faq.a: No, I'm not a software engineering lead and I don't build custom apps. I help owners choose, connect and automate the business software they already have. If you need custom development, you should hire a developer or a CTO with an engineering background.

CRM integration means connecting your CRM to your other tools so data flows automatically. For example, a web form creates a lead, the lead gets a follow-up text, and a won job flows into scheduling and accounting. It cuts double entry and missed follow-ups.
